--help:
usage: code-review-graph [-h] [-v] <command> ...

Persistent incremental knowledge graph for code reviews

positional arguments:
  <command>
    install          Register MCP server with AI coding platforms
    init             Alias for install
    uninstall        Safely remove code-review-graph data, configs, hooks, and
                     generated skills
    doctor           Check which copies run, the graph and the hooks (read-
                     only)
    build            Full graph build (re-parse all files)
    update           Incremental update (only changed files)
    postprocess      Run post-processing on existing graph (flows,
                     communities, FTS)
    embed            Compute vector embeddings for semantic search
    watch            Watch for changes and auto-update
    status           Show graph statistics
    context-history  Show the opt-in context savings log as a per-day or per-
                     tool trend
    forget           Remove already-parsed files from the graph without a full
                     rebuild
    visualize        Generate an interactive HTML graph visualisation
    wiki             Generate markdown wiki from community structure
    register         Register a repository in the multi-repo registry
    unregister       Remove a repository from the multi-repo registry
    repos            List registered repositories
    eval             Run evaluation benchmarks
    detect-changes   Analyse change impact against the existing graph (read-
                     only). Does NOT re-parse files — for that, use 'update
                     --brief'.
    dead-code        Find functions/classes with no callers or test references
    query            Query graph relationships
    impact           Analyse the blast radius of changes
    search           Search graph entities
    flows            List stored execution flows
    flow             Show one stored execution flow
    communities      List graph communities
    community        Show one graph community
    architecture     Show architecture overview
    large-functions  Find oversized graph nodes
    refactor         Preview graph-backed refactors
    serve            Start MCP server (stdio by default, or HTTP on localhost
                     with --http)
    mcp              Alias for serve
    daemon           Multi-repo watch daemon (start/stop/status/add/remove)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  -v, --version      Show version and exit

Start: code-review-graph install && code-review-graph build

                                      [--repo REPO]

  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --detail-level {minimal,standard}
  --repo REPO           Repository root (auto-detected)
build:
usage: code-review-graph build [-h] [--repo REPO] [-q] [--skip-flows]
                               [--skip-postprocess] [--data-dir DATA_DIR]
                               [--embedding-provider {local,openai,google,minimax,voyage}]
                               [--embedding-model EMBEDDING_MODEL]
                               [--follow-symlinks | --no-follow-symlinks]
                               [--enrich] [--wait]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo REPO           Repository root (auto-detected)
  -q, --quiet           Suppress output
  --skip-flows          Skip flow/community detection (signatures + FTS only)
  --skip-postprocess    Skip all post-processing (raw parse only)
  --data-dir DATA_DIR   External directory to store graph database (useful for
                        network shares)
  --embedding-provider {local,openai,google,minimax,voyage}
                        Explicitly refresh an existing embedding index with
                        this provider; requires --embedding-model (default:
                        disabled)
  --embedding-model EMBEDDING_MODEL
                        Exact model for --embedding-provider. Cloud providers
                        may transmit source-derived text and incur API cost
  --follow-symlinks, --no-follow-symlinks
                        Also index files in symlinked folders, inside or
                        outside the repository, stored under their path inside
                        it. Links that loop are skipped, and at most
                        CRG_MAX_FOLLOWED_FILES files are taken. Default: off,
                        or CRG_FOLLOW_SYMLINKS
  --enrich              Also resolve Python method calls with Jedi (needs the
                        'enrichment' extra; about a second more per Python
                        file). Same as CRG_ENABLE_ENRICHMENT=1. Default: off
  --wait                If a build for this repository is already running,
                        wait for it to finish instead of skipping. Default:
                        report the overlap and exit without re-parsing the
                        same files.

detect-changes:
usage: code-review-graph detect-changes [-h] [--base BASE] [--brief]
                                        [--repo REPO] [--churn] [--verify]
                                        [--details SECTIONS]

options:
  -h, --help          show this help message and exit
  --base BASE         Git diff base (branch refs use their merge base with
                      HEAD; default: HEAD~1)
  --brief             Show the risk summary + Token Savings panel instead of
                      the full JSON. Read-only against the existing graph.
  --repo REPO         Repository root (auto-detected)
  --churn             Add an opt-in change-frequency term to risk scores.
                      Counts commits per file over 90 days by default; set
                      CRG_CHURN_WINDOW_DAYS to adjust.
  --verify            Calibrate the estimated savings against tiktoken's
                      cl100k_base tokenizer (the GPT-4 family tokenizer). Adds
                      a second row to the panel with the real token counts.
                      Requires `pip install tiktoken`.
  --details SECTIONS  Add bounded graph context to the JSON under 'details': a
                      comma-separated list of risk, communities, hubs,
                      coupling, impact, gaps, graph, or all. Not used with
                      --brief.
doctor:
usage: code-review-graph doctor [-h] [--repo REPO] [--json]

Check the setup without changing anything: every code-review-graph on PATH and
its version, the version the MCP entries in this repository's configs run, the
graph's schema and whether it is current, and which hooks are installed. Exit
0 when nothing failed, 1 when something did.

  --repo REPO  Repository root (auto-detected)
  --json       Output one machine-readable JSON object

neighbourhood view:
  Draw a neighbourhood instead of the whole repository. Seeded views carry
  only the nodes within --depth hops of the seed; everything else is left
  out of the payload, not dimmed.

  --seed-symbol SYMBOL  Seed from a symbol (qualified name, 'file.py::name',
                        or a bare name). Repeatable.
  --seed-file PATH      Seed from a file and its symbols; glob patterns
                        allowed. Repeatable.
  --seed-changed        Seed from the files changed against --seed-changed-
                        base
  --seed-changed-base REF
                        Git ref --seed-changed diffs against (default: HEAD~1)
  --seed-flow FLOW      Seed from an execution flow (name or id); see 'flows'
  --path-from SYMBOL    Start symbol of a shortest-path query
  --path-to SYMBOL      End symbol of a shortest-path query; the path through
                        CALLS, IMPORTS_FROM and INHERITS is highlighted
  --depth K             Hops of context to include around the seed (default:
                        2)
  --render-depth K      Hops drawn before expanding on click (default: 1)
  --max-nodes N         Hard cap on payload nodes. The outermost hop is
                        trimmed first; once the outer hops are gone the seed
                        set is trimmed too, so the cap always holds (default:
                        1500)
  --sidecar             Write the payload to graph.data.js next to the page
                        instead of inlining it. Off by default: the default
                        output is one self-contained file
